chapter: Childhood, first drums and the hustling years
title: Living with Lil and Louis Armstrong in Chicago
summary: His sister was a childhood friend of Lil Armstrong, so the family stayed with Lil and Louis after they married in 1924; he recalls their late hours, the Savoy Five and its classic records.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Right, right, right, right. And then, when we first come to Chicago, in -- around '23, was the heyday of Lil Armstrong, who was from Memphis, and she and my sister were very, very close friends there, they were real buddy-buddy girls.
Did your sister know Lil in Memphis?

Yeah, that's what I'm saying, in Memphis -- they went to school in -- elementary school together. All the way through school, and when I come here, then I stayed with them for awhile. We stayed with Lil and Louis. They had just gotten married. They got married in '24.
Uh-huh, and we stayed with them, you know, for awhile.
What do you remember from that time of living with Louis and Lil?

Well, during that time, they -- Chicago was such a musical town and there was so much music going on, and then they were working night clubs, you know, because she was in the Dreamland Cafe then. And so -
But she got the gig there and Louis came back --
And Louis -- yeah, and she met him and had to work with him.

Yeah, right, see, so their association -- I mean, I was just going to school and then I didn't have too much because they were working -- they would work til 3:00 or 4:00 in the morning, and then they got home, and then the musicians in those days were really happy-go-lucky guys. Maybe they'd get home at 12:00 and maybe not. But it was -- that was the earliest association with them, and then --
Do you remember Louis practicing or anything at home?
Not too much then, but I remember how he had to -- how he used to scuffle, and when he left the Savoy and then he had the Savoy Five, and they used to play these dances up at the Warwick Hall.
Oh, with Zutty [Singleton] and Earl Hines.
Right, Earl and Zutty, and they made classic records that they had made. Those are classics today.
Well, it was the avant garde of its time.
When Louis played, that was -- that's still some wild --
